items.sentence: A typical example has a body shell surrounding its passenger cabin, with doors and windows providing access and outward visibility.
Many enclosed passenger models provide two to five seats, with restraints arranged around occupants inside the cabin.
Four road wheels usually support the chassis, while springs and dampers reduce jolts reaching the passenger compartment.
Propulsion may come from a gasoline or diesel engine, a hybrid system, or a battery-powered electric motor.
The operator turns a steering wheel to guide the front wheels and change the vehicle's direction along the road.
Pressing the accelerator increases requested propulsion, while applying the brake slows the vehicle through friction or energy recovery.
Before moving, occupants typically fasten seat belts and the operator selects a gear or drive setting.
Turn signals flash before a turn or lane change, indicating the operator's intended movement to nearby road users.
On public streets, enclosed passenger vehicles travel in mixed traffic and must follow applicable signals and speed limits.
In cold weather, occupants can use cabin heating and window defogging to maintain comfort and improve visibility.
At service stops, drivers may replenish liquid fuel, while battery-powered versions can connect to charging equipment.
In crowded urban districts, motorists may spend considerable time searching for a permitted parking space.
An enclosed road vehicle provides private, door-to-door transportation for individuals or small groups traveling along streets and highways.
Its cabin offers a protected place for shopping bags, luggage, and work equipment during journeys.
Specially equipped versions help emergency medical crews reach patients and transport personnel or supplies.
Personal access to an enclosed passenger vehicle can make distant workplaces and services reachable when destinations are spread across a region.
